newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore says economic recovery under way.
newsitem.headline: Singapore says economic recovery under way.

text.p: Singapore Trade and Industry Minister Lee Yock Suan said on Thursday Singapore's economic recovery was under way and repeated the government's economic growth forecast for 1997 of 5.0-7.0 percent.
"We still say five to seven percent for this year," Lee told reporters after presiding over the announcement of a new wafer fabrication plant in Singapore.
He quoted the U.S. semiconductor industry's book-to-bill ratio, which measures shipments against future orders, as showing the global electronics industry was turning around.

Singapore is heavily dependent on the electronics industry. Electronics and computer components make up almost 50 percent of the country's manufacturing output and around 60 percent of its non-oil exports.
"The book-to-bill ratio is positive. It shows the orders are more than the shipments. The leading indicators are also positive. That usually tells us that recovery is under way," Lee said.
Lee declined to comment on the performance of the Singapore economy in the first quarter of 1997.
Singapore's industrial production fell 7.2 percent in January against January 1995, partly reflecting the widespread slowdown in the global electronics industry last year.
But Lee said he was confident of a recovery in the country's core electronics sector despite figures showing a drop of 3.1 percent year-on-year in electronics exports.
"We are confident, despite the setback," he said.

Lee said earlier in a speech that the Singapore government had identified electronics wafer fabrication as a strategic industry which would provide high returns for the country's skilled but limited workforce.

Wafer fabrication plants are central to the production of the micro-chips that control modern electronics. The plants take thin round wafers of silicon, coat them with various metals and print or etch on circuits. The wafers are later cut up into tiny chips for use in computers, telephones and other devices.
"Just over four years ago, Singapore had only four wafer fab plants. Today we have 10 plants that are either already in operation or under development," Lee said.
The minister rejected suggestions that Singapore was over-dependent on the electronics sector and had all its industrial "eggs in one basket".

"On the whole we are still very confident of the industry and we think it is the right industry to have, especially wafer fab plants. We would like to build up our capacity in this area," Lee told reporters.
"It is really a key component of a lot of new products and advances in technology are very rapid. What we intend to have is a lot of state-of-the-art plants.

"The situation in many countries shows that the electronics industry is really the growth sector with the advent of the micro-chip and the enormous potential that has opened up. It reflects the nature of the technology in the world market."

"We do have also other sectors like the chemical industry and petrochemicals and we are pushing the other sectors as well. The fact that it is one of the biggest sectors is just a natural positive development. It is the same in any country."
